subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLO checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLO checklist & next steps

Hi Alice / Rahul,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the time. As promised, attaching a short SLO checklist so we can capture targets and agree on a MAP (mutual action plan) for the performance validation run. Please review the items below and confirm your targets and any constraints.

Quick recap of asks from today's call:
- Primary latency target: P95 <= 200ms (app-level, end-to-end)
- Tail concerns: P99 target / acceptable burst behavior
- Throughput: baseline 500 req/s, peak 1,000 req/s (bursty)
- Concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent connections for streaming endpoints
- Streaming: must support incremental token streaming to client (SSE/websocket acceptable)
- Payloads: average prompt 60 tokens (text), typical output 120 tokens

Next steps (proposed MAP):
1) FintechCo to confirm targets and provide representative payloads (owner: FintechCo) — attached sample payloads welcome
2) Redwood to run a 2-hour performance validation in our staging with agreed model/config (owner: Redwood SE)
3) Capture token-level cost and latency reports, review and iterate (owner: joint)
4) If pass, scope Dedicated sizing and contract terms (owner: Sales)

Attachments: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (fill in your target numbers and any notes)

Can you confirm the P95/P99 numbers and whether the streaming requirements apply to all routes or just the chat endpoint? Also propose 2x slots for the perf run next week — we can do Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLO checklist & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side after internal alignment: 

> On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 3:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Quick recap of asks from today's call:
> > - Primary latency target: P95 <= 200ms (app-level, end-to-end)
> > - Tail concerns: P99 target / acceptable burst behavior

- P95 target: we can set the initial target to P95 <= 250ms (app-level). If the perf run shows room, we'll tighten to 200ms as a stretch.
- P99: we'd like P99 <= 800ms (soft requirement) given occasional heavy context windows.
- Throughput: baseline 400 req/s, peak 800 req/s.
- Concurrency: plan for 150 concurrent streaming connections (chat) initially.
- Streaming: required for chat endpoint only (not for batch embedding endpoints).

I've attached a zip with representative payloads and three sample conversation traces: fintech-payloads.zip.

We're available for a perf run on Tue 2027-04-06 09:00-11:00 PST or Wed 2027-04-07 09:00-11:00 PST. Please confirm which slot works for your SE.

Regards,
Alice Johnson
Director of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
alice.johnson@fintechco.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance SLO checklist & next steps (technical clarifications)

Thanks team — looping in a few technical clarifications before we lock the perf window.

Summary notes / questions for FintechCo (to confirm):
- Request shape: are these single-turn chat requests or multi-turn with long context? Alice mentioned "conversation traces" — what's the max context tokens we should test?
- Avg prompt size: 60 tokens / avg response 120 tokens (Marissa's note) — please confirm distribution (P10/P50/P90).
- Embeddings & batch endpoints: are we excluding embeddings from streaming tests? (Marissa / Alice: confirmed embeddings are not streaming)
- Model variant: we'll propose redwood-medium-8q for initial perf-run (8-bit quantized) unless you need top-tier quality — call that out if so.
- Batching: Redwood runtime supports dynamic batching; for streaming endpoints we use small batches/continuous flush to preserve latency. For non-streaming endpoints we can batch more aggressively.

Preliminary config we recommend for Tue run:
- Model: redwood-medium-8q
- Concurrency target: simulate 150 streaming clients, ramp to 400 rps for non-streaming routes
- Measurement: capture P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, GPU memory, tokens/sec, tail latency over 2-hour window
- Streaming test: chunk size ~32 tokens with SSE; measure time-to-first-token and per-token spacing

I've uploaded our perf-run playbook here: https://internal.redwood.com/playbooks/perf-run (internal link) — will share run script once payloads are ingested.

If FintechCo confirms the Tue slot (2027-04-06 09:00 PST) we'll schedule the run and post the run report within 24 hours.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
